angles.zSignedHint: Slider runs from −180° to +180°. Crossing zero physically flips the telescope through the zenith, but face (L/R) and the alidade are NOT touched. To rotate the alidade 180° and switch face, use the Flip button on the left.

zenith.intro: Flip through zenith and visualize the doubled collimation error.
zenith.markerEmpty: Aim the sight → "Mark point 1". Then move the sight (slider, or the Flip button to switch face) and hit "Mark point 2".
zenith.markerHalf: Point 1 pinned. Move the sight any way (z slider, HA slider, or the Flip button) and press "Mark point 2".
zenith.markerHint: The two scene markers are the actual sight tip before and after the flip. The segment between them is the doubled collimation error 2c/sin z.
zenith.explanation: Averaging face L and R cancels collimation error c. VV tilt survives averaging.

formulas.collimation: ΔHA = ±c / sin z. Sign flips on face R — two-face averaging cancels c.
formulas.index: z = V − i on face L; z = (2π − V) − i on face R. Averaging both faces cancels i.
formulas.tilt: ΔHA = (tiltX·sin HA − tiltY·cos HA)·cot z. Not cancelled by two-face averaging.

stop0.title: What is a theodolite?
stop0.body: A theodolite is a surveying instrument for measuring horizontal (HA) and vertical (z) angles. Its design is built around three mutually perpendicular axes. Let's look at each one.

stop1.title: Vertical axis VV
stop1.body: VV is the main instrument axis — ideally vertical when the instrument is levelled. The alidade rotates about it. The horizontal angle HA measures that rotation. Try dragging the HA slider and watch the alidade move.

stop2.title: Trunnion axis HH
stop2.body: HH is perpendicular to VV and passes through the telescope. The telescope rotates about HH, determining zenith distance z. The ideal condition is HH ⊥ VV.

stop3.title: Sight axis ZZ
stop3.body: ZZ is the optical axis of the telescope, pointed at the target. Ideally ZZ ⊥ HH. Any deviation is the collimation error c. Enable the Sight Line and try changing c on its slider.

stop4.title: Reading the angles
stop4.body: HA is read from the horizontal circle. Zenith distance z is read from the vertical circle. The arcs show both angles simultaneously. Try the HA and z sliders and watch the arcs change.

measure.noTargets: No targets. Enable Place mode and click the scene.

hints.HA: Horizontal angle — rotation of the alidade about the vertical axis VV. Read from the horizontal circle.
hints.z: Zenith distance — telescope angle from vertical (zenith). z = 90° means the telescope is horizontal.
hints.c: Collimation error: angle between sight axis ZZ and the plane perpendicular to HH. Cancelled by two-face averaging.
hints.i: Vertical index error: constant offset of the vertical circle zero. Cancelled by averaging face L and face R readings.
hints.tiltX: VV tilt across the line of sight. Affects HA; NOT cancelled by two-face averaging.
hints.tiltY: VV tilt along the line of sight. Affects HA; NOT cancelled by two-face averaging.
